ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, on the left is a 120 V independent voltage source, and the upper end of the source is connected through a 10 Ω series resistor to the left port of the two-port network; the two-port network is represented by a gray box, with [Y] marked inside; the right port is externally connected to the load impedance Z_L. Reasoning: For Z_L to obtain maximum power, Z_L should be taken equal to the Thevenin equivalent impedance looking in from the load terminal. When finding the output-terminal equivalent impedance, suppress the independent voltage source, that is, short-circuit the 120 V voltage source. At this time, the left 10 Ω resistor is equivalent to a parallel conductance connected to port 1, G_s = 1/10 = 0.1 S. From the Y parameters given in the problem: y11 = 2/100 = 0.02 S, y12 = y21 = -1/100 = -0.01 S, y22 = (4/3)/100 = 1/75 S. After port 1 is connected to the parallel conductance G_s, the driving-point admittance looking in from port 2 is: Y_th = y22 - (y21 y12)/(y11 + G_s). Substituting the values: Y_th = 1/75 - [(-0.01)(-0.01)]/(0.02 + 0.1) = 0.0133333 - 0.0001/0.12 = 0.0125 S. Therefore Z_th = 1/Y_th = 1/0.0125 = 80 Ω. The network parameters are all real numbers, so for maximum power transfer Z_L = Z_th = 80 Ω.

raw_record.question_text:
For the two-port network shown below, the \([Y]\)-parameters are given as 
\[
[Y] = \frac{1}{100} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & \frac{4}{3} \end{bmatrix} S
\]
The value of load impedance \(Z_L\), in \(\Omega\), for maximum power transfer will be ___ (rounded off to the nearest integer).

method.method_draft: First describe the image: a 120 V source and 10 Ω series resistor drive the left port of the two-port, and Z_L is connected at the right port. To find the load for maximum power, suppress the independent voltage source, making the 10 Ω resistor a shunt at port 1. From the text, read y11=2/100=0.02 S, y12=y21=-1/100=-0.01 S, y22=(4/3)/100=1/75 S. Add Gs=0.1 S at port 1 and compute the output driving-point admittance: Y_th = y22 - (y21*y12)/(y11+Gs) = 1/75 - 0.0001/0.12 = 0.0125 S. Hence Z_th=1/Y_th=80 Ω, so choose Z_L=80 Ω.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中左侧是一个 120 V 独立电压源，源上端通过一个 10 Ω 串联电阻接到两端口网络的左端口；两端口网络用灰色方框表示，内部标有 [Y]；右端口外接负载阻抗 Z_L。

推理：要求 Z_L 获得最大功率，应取 Z_L 等于从负载端看进去的 Thevenin 等效阻抗。求输出端等效阻抗时，抑制独立电压源，即把 120 V 电压源短路。此时左侧 10 Ω 电阻等效为接在端口 1 上的并联电导 G_s = 1/10 = 0.1 S。

由题给 Y 参数：y11 = 2/100 = 0.02 S，y12 = y21 = -1/100 = -0.01 S，y22 = (4/3)/100 = 1/75 S。

端口 1 接入并联电导 G_s 后，从端口 2 看进去的驱动点导纳为：Y_th = y22 - (y21 y12)/(y11 + G_s)。代入数值：Y_th = 1/75 - [(-0.01)(-0.01)]/(0.02 + 0.1) = 0.0133333 - 0.0001/0.12 = 0.0125 S。

因此 Z_th = 1/Y_th = 1/0.0125 = 80 Ω。网络参数均为实数，所以最大功率传输时 Z_L = Z_th = 80 Ω。

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the two-port block has a left input driven through 10 Ω and a right output terminated by Z_L. From the text, interpret the Y matrix as a passive pi network: the admittance between ports is Y_bridge=-y12=0.01 S, so R_bridge=100 Ω; the left shunt is y11-Y_bridge=0.02-0.01=0.01 S, so 100 Ω; the right shunt is y22-Y_bridge=1/75-0.01=1/300 S, so 300 Ω. Suppress the 120 V source shown in the image, so the input node has 10 Ω in parallel with the 100 Ω left shunt: 10||100=9.0909 Ω. Looking from the output, one path is the 300 Ω shunt, and the other path is 100 Ω bridge plus 9.0909 Ω to ground, i.e. 109.0909 Ω. Thus R_th = 300 || 109.0909 = 80 Ω. Therefore the maximum-power load is Z_L=80 Ω.

推理：给定 [Y] = (1/100) [[2, -1], [-1, 4/3]] S，因此 y11 = 0.02 S，y12 = y21 = -0.01 S，y22 = 1/75 S。按无源 π 型等效网络解释，端口间桥接导纳为 y_bridge = -y12 = 0.01 S，对应电阻 100 Ω。左侧并联导纳为 y11 - y_bridge = 0.02 - 0.01 = 0.01 S，对应 100 Ω。右侧并联导纳为 y22 - y_bridge = 1/75 - 0.01 = 1/300 S，对应 300 Ω。

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: For the two-port network shown below, the \([Y]\)-parameters are given as \[ [Y] = \frac{1}{100} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ -1 & \frac{4}{3} \end{bmatrix} S \] The value of load impedance \(Z_L\), in \(\Omega\), for maximum power transfer will be ___ (rounded off to the nearest integer).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, on the left is a 120 V independent voltage source, and the upper end of the source is connected through a 10 Ω series resistor to the left port of the two-port network; the two-port network is represented by a gray box, with [Y] marked inside; the right port is externally connected to the load impedance Z_L.

Reasoning: For Z_L to obtain maximum power, Z_L should be taken equal to the Thevenin equivalent impedance looking in from the load terminal. When finding the output-terminal equivalent impedance, suppress the independent voltage source, that is, short-circuit the 120 V voltage source. At this time, the left 10 Ω resistor is equivalent to a parallel conductance connected to port 1, G_s = 1/10 = 0.1 S.

From the Y parameters given in the problem: y11 = 2/100 = 0.02 S, y12 = y21 = -1/100 = -0.01 S, y22 = (4/3)/100 = 1/75 S.

After port 1 is connected to the parallel conductance G_s, the driving-point admittance looking in from port 2 is: Y_th = y22 - (y21 y12)/(y11 + G_s). Substituting the values: Y_th = 1/75 - [(-0.01)(-0.01)]/(0.02 + 0.1) = 0.0133333 - 0.0001/0.12 = 0.0125 S.

Therefore Z_th = 1/Y_th = 1/0.0125 = 80 Ω. The network parameters are all real numbers, so for maximum power transfer Z_L = Z_th = 80 Ω.
